asOf: Updated Sun 20 Sep 2026, 11:56 Dubai · prices from 2026-09-18 close · for the Mon 21 Sep session
kicker: Dubai desk · US open 5:30pm Dubai (9:30am ET)
notes: Fed delivered its first rate hike in three years on Sept 17 (25bp) and signaled more tightening may follow, with markets pricing high odds of another move by the Oct 28/Dec 9 meetings.
10-year Treasury yield has pushed above 5% (highest since 2007) and the Bank of Japan hiked to 1.25%, its highest since 1995, adding to a global tightening backdrop.

Crude remains historically elevated (WTI ~$99-100, Brent ~$103) on the ongoing US-Iran war and Strait of Hormuz disruption, though prices have eased slightly as Saudi Arabia works to restore pipeline flows.
Bitcoin is trading near $81K, up roughly 5% on the week, shrugging off both the Fed hike and the Senate's failure to pass crypto market-structure legislation (Clarity Act) on Sept 16.

Equity tape is choppy: Nasdaq finished the week higher on a semiconductor rebound after an early-week selloff tied to AI-labs calling for a slowdown in frontier model development, while the Dow lost over 1.5% on rate jit

Geopolitical risk stays high heading into Monday: Iran says the Strait of Hormuz stays closed until its conditions are met, and Houthi-Saudi fighting has flared near Riyadh, keeping an energy/defense bid in the market.
calendar: Earnings docket is thin Monday (no major reports); heavier days are Tuesday (AutoZone, General Mills, KB Home, Cintas) and Thursday (Darden, Costco, Paychex, Lennar, TD Synnex).

IPO watch: Orion180 (OIG) began trading Sept 18 at $12 and closed its debut week roughly 2-3% below issue price; CVC-backed Bamboo Insurance is slated to go public next week targeting a ~$3.24B valuation.
M&A/contract flow to track: Copart's $1.9B deal for ACV Auctions, the $7.7B take-private of The Baldwin Group, and Independence Realty's $2.14B acquisition of Centerspace remain in the news cycle.
Fed speakers and any Middle East ceasefire/escalation headlines are the key macro swing factors this week given the thin earnings calendar.
Carry-over analyst actions from Friday session (JPMorgan upgrades on Tyson and Recursion, BTIG upgrade on Etsy, Tigress price-target hike on Intel) are likely to still be in focus Monday morning.
